rv.q: It’s an injection of fun into the sometimes overly earnest American theater.
Karen Zacarías’s soap opera spoof pairs catchy music with sharp truths about Latinos in America.
Karen Zacarías’ “Destiny of Desire: A Telenovela Play With Music” at the Mark Taper Forum is one of the funniest and best experiences you’ll ever have in the theater.
Destiny of Desire is an absolute delight from start to finish.
Live theater doesn’t get any more telenovela -licious than this.
If you are looking for an evening of pure high-energy theatrical joy, look no further than the Taper.
Karen Zacarías’ 2015 comedy “Destiny of Desire” is a telenovela on crack, a hilarious love letter to what makes this brand of soap-opera fabulous...
A carefree romp underscored by a digestible strain of social commentary, Destiny of Desire hits the sweet spot between reality and make-believe.
The result is the funniest show to come around in a long time, judging by the sheer number of laugh-out-loud moments throughout its two-hour-and-20-minute running time.
For at least one night at the Mark Taper Forum, I felt continuity, and I can't begin to describe the comfort of that.

Brimming with energy, Karen Zacarías’ hilarious hit, Destiny of Desire , takes you on an emotional rollercoaster sprinkled with the melodrama and wild antics that make the telenovela the most popular form of storytelling in the world.
Skillfully helmed by Marcela Lorca, DESTINY OF DESIRE is a laugh-out-loud comedy of uproarious proportions.

cn.t: Critics widely embrace this telenovela spoof as a high-energy delight, praising its sharp humor and catchy music. A few note it favors spectacle over substance, but most call it an outrageously fun night out.
